meshy_task.text_style_prompt: Terrapup, a stylised pup creature. Rich chocolate-brown fur (not yellow, not golden), a cream-white blaze down the face, cream muzzle, chest and belly, darker brown ears; teal-blue eyes with white catchlight, dark brown nose. Grey stone plates with olive-green moss on the shoulders, back and tail tip. Paw pads and the underside of the feet are soft warm brown-grey, natural and matte, never black; tan-ivory claws. Matte hand-painted stylised look, clean colour blocks, no noise, no speckle. No red, no pink, no rust, no maroon, no oxblood anywhere.

palette.red_metric: texels with HSV hue <24 or >320 deg, saturation >0.25, value >0.12 (the retex worker clamp rule), over the whole 2048 atlas

transfer.atlas_identity: candidate Image_0 is byte-identical to the recovered model texture (sha256 f34045e2146a4251713f7586df66b6204e81c6fa2fb7c6b108ec106c51e74e63)

uv_check.method: candidate triangle centroids (decimated mesh) projected to the nearest retexture triangle after bbox normalisation and best of 8 yaw/mirror alignments; interpolated UV compared to centroid UV

transfer.uv_check_summary: Decimated candidate UVs sample the retexture atlas consistently: median 0.27 texel error at triangle centroids, 92.2% within 1 texel, 98.8% within 4 texels. The retex worker found retexture (position, UV) pairs match the recovered model 99.99-100% (welds only), and the candidate atlas is byte-identical to the recovered texture, so the maps occupy the exact atlas space the candidate already samples. The remaining centroids are ordinary-sized triangles (median longest UV edge 13.58 texels vs 16.94 for inliers, so not seam-straddling) whose nearest retexture surface after bbox normalisation lies on another UV island (thin or near-coincident sheets); they still sample the same atlas texels the candidate samples with its original Image_0, because the UVs themselves are unchanged.
